fixtures.title: Accessibility page
fixtures.purpose: The reference bar on a page of its own, so a screen-reader pass or an axe run reports on the nav and not on whatever else a shared fixture happens to carry

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Authoring - The logo, the links, and what makes an item a dropdown
tests.scope: What authored content produces on the bar: the logo and its text fallback, at least one link, and the fact that an item becomes a dropdown purely because content was authored under it — there is no switch to set.
tests.findings: Step 5 is expected to fail. The text logo works — the brand name renders and is still a link — but it is 280px wide where the image is 107px, and the extra 173px pushes the last nav item underneath the search field. Confirmed in a browser on FX-04 with the production five items. The underlying cause is that the bar has no overflow strategy at all. The links sit between the logo and the tools with nothing to stop them growing: when the authored labels need more room than is left, they do not wrap, scroll or truncate — they carry on underneath the tools cluster and off the edge of the window. There is no page-level sideways scroll, so the overflowing items are simply unreachable.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-01 and look at the nav bar.
steps.result: The logo sits at the start edge and all five authored items follow it in a single row, in the order they were authored: Products, Recipes, Training & Inspiration, Promotions, Loyalty Program.

steps.action: Still on FX-01, compare the five items to each other.
steps.result: The four items that have content authored under them carry a small chevron next to the label; Loyalty Program, which has none, carries no chevron. Nothing else distinguishes them.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-05, where every item was authored with nothing under it.
steps.result: All five render as ordinary links and not one of them shows a chevron. The bar is otherwise laid out exactly as on FX-01.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-02, which authors a single nav link.
steps.result: The bar renders with the logo at the start and that one link after it. No gap, placeholder or stray separator is left where the other items would have been.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-04, where the logo was authored as text instead of an image.
steps.result: The brand name renders as text in the logo's place and is still a link to the home page. Nothing shifts out of position and no broken-image icon appears.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-03, which authors eight items including several long labels.
steps.result: All eight render, in the authored order, with none dropped or merged. Each label stays on one line.

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Functionality - Hover, opening a dropdown, following a link, and staying pinned
tests.scope: What the bar does when you use it: hover feedback, a dropdown that opens and closes without navigating, a plain link that does navigate, and the bar staying at the top of the screen while the page scrolls.

steps.action: On FX-01, move the pointer onto Recipes and hold it there.
steps.result: The label changes to the hover colour and a coloured line appears under it. Both appear smoothly rather than snapping.

steps.action: Move the pointer off the link.
steps.result: The label and the underline return to their resting state, again smoothly.

steps.action: Click Products.
steps.result: Its dropdown panel opens below the bar and the chevron turns to its open position. The page does NOT navigate — the address bar still shows the fixture page.

steps.action: Click Products a second time.
steps.result: The panel closes and the chevron turns back. Still no navigation.

steps.action: Open Products again, then click Recipes.
steps.result: The Products panel closes and the Recipes panel opens. Only one panel is ever open at a time.

steps.action: Press Escape while a panel is open.
steps.result: The panel closes.

steps.action: On FX-05, click any item.
steps.result: The browser navigates to that item's destination. Nothing opens on the bar first.

steps.action: Back on FX-01, scroll down about three screens.
steps.result: The nav row stays pinned at the very top of the window the whole way down — it never scrolls out of view and never jumps or flickers. The thin utility strip above it slides away as you scroll, which is expected.

steps.action: Keep scrolling to the bottom, then scroll back to the top.
steps.result: The nav row is still pinned and still usable at every point, and the utility strip comes back when you return to the top.

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Visual - Height, colour contexts, the open state, and no clipping
tests.scope: How the bar looks against the approved design: its height and typography, the three colour contexts, what an open dropdown does to the trigger, and that a crowded bar never clips or spills off the page.
tests.findings: Several steps are expected to fail on current code, all of them named in the ticket's own section 8 as work still to do. (a) The nav row measures 70px, not 68px — styles.css sets --nav-h: 70px where the design system sets 68px. (b) The dark and glass contexts do not exist: header.css defines the light treatment only, there is no modifier for the other two and no way for an author to select one, so steps 4, 5 and 7 have nothing to check. (c) The hover/active label colour is #B23E00, from a header-local --hdr-cta-orange, where the design system says --color-orange-700 = #D14900. The repo's own styles.css already defines that token. #B23E00 is the higher-contrast of the two, so raise it as a fidelity question rather than letting anyone 'fix' it back to something that fails AA. (d) Step 8 is expected to fail. On FX-03 at 1440px the fourth label is cut off by the search field and the last three items render behind the tools, off the right edge of the window. The underlying cause is that the bar has no overflow strategy at all. The links sit between the logo and the tools with nothing to stop them growing: when the authored labels need more room than is left, they do not wrap, scroll or truncate — they carry on underneath the tools cluster and off the edge of the window. There is no page-level sideways scroll, so the overflowing items are simply unreachable. Answered 26 Aug by Gianluca Volpe: follow the designs unless doing so breaks an accessibility rule. So 68px and #D14900 stand as the expected values — but #B23E00 is the higher-contrast of the two, so check the design value still meets AA at the label's size before anyone changes the code to it.

steps.action: On FX-01 at 1440px wide, measure the nav row.
steps.result: It is 68px tall. The logo image is 40px tall and sits at the start; the links follow in a row; the tools on the right sit in their own space without pushing the links or overlapping them.

steps.action: Look at the link text.
steps.result: Labels are 14px, weight 600, with 12px of space either side of each one, and none of them wraps.

steps.action: Check the light context, which is the default.
steps.result: The bar is white with a thin hairline under it, and the labels are dark ink (#221D37).

steps.action: Switch the bar to the dark context.
steps.result: The bar background becomes dark ink (#221D37) and the labels become white at 82% opacity. The icons invert so they stay visible.

steps.action: Switch the bar to the glass context and place it over hero media.
steps.result: The bar becomes a blurred gradient over the image behind it, with white labels at 82% opacity and inverted icons. The media stays readable through it.

steps.action: Open the Products dropdown in the light context.
steps.result: A 2px line appears under Products in #FF5A00, its label turns to the hover colour #D14900, and the chevron is in its open position.

steps.action: Open a dropdown in the dark context, then in the glass context.
steps.result: In both, the 2px line under the trigger is #FF5A00 and the label turns white.

steps.action: Open FX-03 and view it at 1440px, 1280px and 1024px.
steps.result: At every width all eight labels are fully readable — nothing is cut off, nothing overlaps the logo or the tools, and the page itself never scrolls sideways.

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Compatibility, desktop - Desktop widths and browsers
tests.scope: The component on the desktop side of the 1024px breakpoint, in every browser we support, plus the breakpoint itself.
tests.findings: The desktop/mobile switch is 900px. Gianluca Volpe answered this on EC-7 on 26 Aug 2026, against the three values that were in play; AC-7 and AC-15 still say 1024px and need correcting to match. header.css switches at 1200px, so steps 3 to 8 are expected to fail from 1199px down to 900px: the hamburger bar shows where the spec calls for the full desktop nav.

steps.action: BrowserStack — small desktop, 1024 wide — Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.
steps.result: Desktop treatment in all four browsers — the full bar: logo, every authored link, and the tools cluster — matching the design reference. Nothing clipped or overlapping, and no sideways scroll. No difference between browsers.

steps.action: BrowserStack — large desktop, 2560 wide or more — Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.
steps.result: As on the small desktop. Text and images scale cleanly: nothing blurred, mis-aligned, or stranded by the extra width. Nothing clipped or overlapping, and no sideways scroll.

steps.action: Small desktop at 1023 wide, then at 1024 wide.
steps.result: 1024 gets the desktop treatment and 1023 gets the mobile one. Crossing the line in either direction loses nothing and duplicates nothing. This step is what pins the breakpoint — none of the real devices we test falls between 900 and 1024, so nothing else would catch it.

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Compatibility, mobile - Tablets and phones
tests.scope: The component on tablets and phones, on the real devices we support rather than a resized desktop window.
tests.findings: Steps 6 and 7 are expected to fail: the switch happens at 1200px, not the 900px Gianluca Volpe confirmed on EC-7 on 26 Aug 2026 — so the mobile bar starts 300px too early. Steps 1 to 5 pass; the mobile bar itself is correct. AC-7 and AC-15 still say 1024px and need correcting to match.

steps.action: BrowserStack — tablets, both orientations — a mid-size iPad in Safari and in Chrome, and a mid-size Android tablet in Chrome.
steps.result: Portrait sits below 1024, so the mobile treatment applies — the hamburger and the logo, with the links behind the drawer. Landscape sits above it, so the desktop treatment applies — the full bar: logo, every authored link, and the tools cluster. Both match the design reference, and everything stays operable by touch. Nothing clipped or overlapping, and no sideways scroll.

steps.action: BrowserStack — phones — the smallest current iPhone in Safari and in Chrome, and the latest Galaxy S in Chrome.
steps.result: The mobile treatment applies — the hamburger and the logo, with the links behind the drawer — matching the design reference. Everything is reachable and operable by touch. The smallest iPhone is the narrowest screen we support, so this is where clipping shows first. Nothing clipped or overlapping, and no sideways scroll.

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Accessibility - Keyboard, focus, and what a screen reader hears
tests.scope: Whether the bar can be used and understood without a mouse: tab order, one stop per item, keys that open and close a dropdown, a focus ring you can actually see, and semantics that describe the bar honestly.
tests.findings: Four steps are expected to fail, and all four are real barriers rather than pedantry. (a) Step 1 — tab order is logo, then the tools on the right, then the nav links, so focus jumps to the far right of the bar and back. (b) Step 2 — every dropdown item takes two Tab stops: the <li> carries tabindex="0" and its <a> is focusable too, and the <li> has no role, so its accessible name is the entire flattened contents of its dropdown. (c) Steps 7 and 8 — there is no focus rule for the top-level links at all, so what you see is Chrome's default blue outline, not --color-accessible-orange. (d) Steps 9 and 10 — aria-expanded is set on the <li>, which is a listitem and does not support it, so it never reaches assistive technology; the focusable <a> has neither aria-expanded nor aria-haspopup. On top of that the whole bar sits inside .nav-drawer, which carries role="dialog" aria-label="Main menu" and display: contents — so at desktop widths a screen reader announces the entire primary navigation as a dialog that visually is not there. Confirmed from the browser's accessibility tree.

steps.action: Open FX-07, click once in the address bar, then press Tab repeatedly through the header.
steps.result: Focus moves in the order things appear on screen: the logo first, then each nav link left to right, then the tools on the right. Nothing is skipped and nothing is reached out of order.

steps.action: Count the Tab presses it takes to move from one top-level item to the next.
steps.result: One press per item. No item takes two stops, and no stop lands on something that is not a control.

steps.action: Tab to Loyalty Program and press Enter.
steps.result: The browser navigates to it, the same as a click would.

steps.action: Go back, Tab to Products, and press Enter. Then press Space on it.
steps.result: Either key opens the dropdown. The page does not navigate.

steps.action: With the dropdown open, press Escape.
steps.result: It closes and focus stays on Products, so you can carry on tabbing from where you were.

steps.action: Keep pressing Tab past the end of the nav.
steps.result: Focus leaves the header and continues into the page. Nothing traps it.

steps.action: Look at the focus ring on each item as you tab through.
steps.result: Every focused item shows a clearly visible ring in #D14900 (--color-accessible-orange), not the browser's own default outline.

steps.action: Repeat the tab-through with the bar in the dark context, then the glass context.
steps.result: The ring stays clearly visible against both backgrounds.

steps.action: Inspect a dropdown trigger with the browser's accessibility panel, closed and then open.
steps.result: The element you actually focus reports aria-expanded, false when closed and true when open. The chevron is marked aria-hidden. The logo link has an accessible name, and the hamburger has a label.

steps.action: Read the whole header with a screen reader.
steps.result: It is announced as a navigation region. Each item is announced by its own label only — never by the whole contents of its dropdown — and nothing in the bar is announced as a dialog.

steps.action: Run axe-core on FX-07 and note anything reported inside the header.
steps.result: No new violations. Link, hover and active text all meet WCAG AA contrast against each of the three context backgrounds.

steps.action: Run Lighthouse on FX-07 and read the accessibility score.
steps.result: 100, unless something outside the header is responsible — check what it names before recording a failure.

tests.summary: Header: Navigation - Internationalization - Right-to-left and long labels
tests.scope: The bar in a right-to-left market, authored in Arabic rather than reversed English: everything mirrors except the chevrons, which the spec deliberately leaves alone. Also that labels longer than English ones do not break the row.
tests.findings: Step 6 is expected to fail for the same reason as NAV-TC-03 step 8, not because of anything to do with German. The long label does render on one line without wrapping, but on FX-03 it runs under the search field and is cut off there. The underlying cause is that the bar has no overflow strategy at all. The links sit between the logo and the tools with nothing to stop them growing: when the authored labels need more room than is left, they do not wrap, scroll or truncate — they carry on underneath the tools cluster and off the edge of the window. There is no page-level sideways scroll, so the overflowing items are simply unreachable. Steps 1 to 5 and 8 pass: mirroring is correct, the logo moves to the right start edge, the links run right to left in the authored order, and the chevrons keep their unmirrored rotation exactly as AC-9 asks.

steps.action: Open the Arabic fixture on small desktop at 1024, in Chrome, and look at the nav bar.
steps.result: The page is in Arabic and reads right to left — dir="rtl" and the Arabic locale in lang.

steps.action: Compare it against the RTL section of the design reference.
steps.result: Mirrored as the design shows, and anything that section says must NOT mirror keeps its left-to-right treatment.

steps.action: Repeat on large desktop, on both tablets in both orientations, and on both phones.
steps.result: It mirrors correctly at every size, with the correct treatment either side of 1024. Nothing clipped at either edge, and no sideways scroll.

steps.action: Open a dropdown.
steps.result: It anchors to the mirrored bar and stays on screen. The chevrons keep their unmirrored rotation, which AC-9 asks for deliberately.

steps.action: Open the long-label fixture on small desktop and on a phone.
steps.result: Every label is fully readable at both sizes. Longer words wrap or truncate as the design shows rather than clipping, overlapping a neighbour, or forcing the page sideways.
